record.paper_title: Open Questions about Ramsey-Type Statements in Reverse Mathematics
record.original_question: In the setting of ω-models of second-order arithmetic, does the stable Ramsey theorem for pairs with two colors imply full Ramsey's theorem for pairs with two colors, equivalently the cohesiveness principle COH?

evidence.quote: Definition 2.2 (Cohesiveness) An infinite set C is R~ -cohesive for a sequence of sets R0, R1, . . . if for each i ∈ N, C ⊆∗ Ri or C ⊆∗ Ri . ... COH is the statement “Every uniform sequence of sets R~ has an R~ -cohesive set.”

Question 2.3 Does SRT2 2 imply RT2 2 (or equivalently COH) over ω-models?
UPDATE: This question was answered negatively by Monin and Patey in [48]

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in second-order arithmetic. An ω-model is a structure of second-order arithmetic whose first-order part is the standard natural numbers ℕ and whose second-order part is some collection S ⊆ 𝒫(ℕ) (closed under the relevant base theory RCA₀).

For sets A, B ⊆ ℕ, write A ⊆* B to mean A ∖ B is finite. Given a sequence R⃗ = ⟨Rᵢ : i ∈ ℕ⟩ of subsets of ℕ, an infinite set C ⊆ ℕ is said to be R⃗-cohesive if for every i ∈ ℕ, either C ⊆* Rᵢ or C ⊆* ℕ ∖ Rᵢ. The cohesiveness principle COH asserts: for every uniformly computable sequence R⃗ of subsets of ℕ, there exists an R⃗-cohesive set.

Ramsey's theorem for pairs with two colors, RT²₂, asserts that for every coloring c : [ℕ]² → {0,1} there is an infinite set H ⊆ ℕ that is homogeneous for c (i.e., c is constant on [H]²). A coloring c : [ℕ]² → {0,1} is stable if for every x ∈ ℕ, lim_{y→∞} c(x,y) exists. The stable Ramsey theorem for pairs with two colors, SRT²₂, is the restriction of RT²₂ to stable colorings.

Question: Does every ω-model of SRT²₂ (over RCA₀) satisfy RT²₂? Equivalently (given the known decomposition RT²₂ ↔ SRT²₂ + COH over ω-models of RCA₀), does SRT²₂ imply COH over ω-models?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered negatively by Benoit Monin and Ludovic Patey in their paper "SRT²₂ does not imply RT²₂ in ω-models" (arXiv:1905.08427, 2019). They construct an ω-model of SRT²₂ that is not a model of RT²₂, using a refined notion of effective Mathias forcing based on largeness classes.

status_evidence.title: SRT22 does not imply RT22 in omega-models
status_evidence.snippet: We construct an ω-model of SRT^2_2 which is not a model of RT^2_2, thereby answering the remaining question on the computability-theoretic analysis of Ramsey's theorem for pairs.
status_evidence.claim: Monin and Patey resolved the question negatively by constructing an ω-model of SRT²₂ that fails to satisfy RT²₂.

status_evidence.title: SRT2_2 DOES NOT IMPLY RT2_2 IN ω-MODELS — Monin and Patey
status_evidence.snippet: We construct an ω-model of SRT^2_2 which is not a model of RT^2_2.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the negative resolution of whether SRT²₂ implies RT²₂ over ω-models.
